article.headline: Quiet Friday: the tape stretches and [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] goes shopping
paras: Not a snap was played on Friday, and the floor moved anyway. The projections shuffled overnight, and the six tenths of a point between the two bottom chairs stretched to a little over three. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] still sleeps on the bottom, now projected 101.6 with a Chop% of 26, up two and a half since Thursday's bell. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] drifted up to a projected 104.7 and watched its Chop% slip to 20. Same chairs, more daylight between them. Somebody check whether the tape measure is long enough.

The only move in the league came from the cheap seats. In the small hours of Friday, [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]], who did not dress a single Thursday starter, won a waiver claim for [[p:12474|Woody Marks (RB, HOU, #4)]] at 4 FAAB and sent Zach Charbonnet to the showers to make room. Marks skates straight into the Sunday late lineup, projected 16.4. A hockey guy at a football game may not know the rules, but he does know how to make a line change.

On paper, the line change worked. Hockey Guy slid two chairs toward the safe end of the room, from sixth to fourth, with a Chop% of 6, down nearly three. [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] went the other way without leaving the hangar: from second to fifth, projected 118.2, Chop% of 6, a little turbulence on an otherwise grounded afternoon. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] stayed parked in eighth at a projected 108.8 and a Chop% of 15, all seven starters still waiting on Sunday.

Up top, nothing to see. [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] keeps the 22.5 it banked Thursday and leads at a projected 127.3 with a Chop% that still rounds to 1. No trades, no other claims, no injuries. Nineteen managers stood pat and stared at the two floor-sitters. One went shopping.

Sunday morning, both floor-sitters wake up at once. outsiderightfoot opens with four early starters and still keeps [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] in its back pocket for late Monday, projected 22.8, the last card anyone at the bottom gets to play. The Naber answers with three in the early window, two late, and [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] under the Sunday night lights, projected 21.4, the policy's biggest premium.
Three points now. Two days of waiting. Bring the tape measure, and maybe a receipt.

articles.headline: Swift opens the gap to 8.2 as the trapdoor under [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] creaks
paras: Fourteen more minutes, and the organ still plays one hymn. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] sits frozen at 51.9 with nobody left to play, a near-lock to be chopped by our numbers. And the floor above just got farther away: [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] climbed to 60.1, so the gap to the trapdoor is now 8.2, up from 6.4.

The turn came from the choir loft in Chicago. [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] chipped in 1.8, now on 5.1, and the church crowd's projected finish rose to 72.6. That's the opposite of singing backward. [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] holds at 65.2, still waiting on [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]] to warm up from 5.7.

Q2, 0:57 to halftime. Torn-Again still has Swift and [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]] on stage. For the next chapter to flip, Rise to the top needs the whole choir to lose its voice and the scoreboard to run backward by more than 8.2. [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] remains on the couch, and the Zamboni has officially been declared missing.

articles.headline: Halftime hymn: the gap above [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] stretches to 10.6
paras: The organ plays on, and the trapdoor stays put. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] is still frozen at 51.9 with nobody left to play, a 100% chop by our numbers. The floor above drifted higher again: [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] reached 62.5, so the gap is now 10.6, up from 8.2.

The church crowd added 2.4, all from [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]], now on 8.5. But the loudest noise came from Seattle. Last chapter we were waiting on [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]] to warm up. He did more than warm up: 13.0 in fourteen minutes, now 18.7, and [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] vaulted to 78.2, projected to finish at 92.3. Nicotine-free and still buzzing.

Halftime in Chicago. Torn-Again still has Loveland and [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] to come, projected to close at 75.1. For the next chapter to flip, the scoreboard would have to run backward by more than 10.6. [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] remains on the couch, and the Zamboni search party has been called off for the night.

articles.headline: Third quarter, same hymn: [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still 10.6 short
paras: Fourteen minutes, zero points, zero movement at the bottom. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] sits on 51.9 with nobody left to play, still a 100% chop by our numbers. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] hasn't budged from 62.5, so the gap holds at 10.6. The halftime organ solo simply ran long.

Now the third quarter is under way, 13:30 on the clock, and every live starter in our league is in this one game. [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] still rides [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]] on 18.7, projected for 32.0. The buzz hasn't worn off. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] and [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] each have a Bear still playing, but both are safely upstairs.

Torn-Again's choir is [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]] on 8.5 and [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] on 5.1, projected to close the night at 74.3. For the next chapter to flip, the church would need the scoreboard to run backward by more than 10.6. Rise to the top remains projected for the chop, and only the clock is left to argue.

articles.headline: The choir finds its voice: [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] now 18.4 short
paras: The organ solo is over, and the church is singing. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] climbed 7.8 points in fourteen minutes to 70.3, while [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still sits on 51.9 with nobody left to play. The gap that held at 10.6 all through halftime is now 18.4. Chop% doesn't move: Rise to the top stays at 100% by our numbers.

The turn came from the back pew. [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] went from 5.1 to 12.9 and turned a hymn into a hallelujah. [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]] holds at 8.5, and Torn-Again is now projected to close the night at 79.6. Upstairs, [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] is still buzzing on [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]] at 18.7, though his projected finish slid to 27.7.

Q3, 5:38, and every live starter in our league is still in this one game. For the next chapter to flip, the scoreboard would have to run backward by 18.4 points, and scoreboards rarely repent. Rise to the top remains projected for the chop, waiting in the pew for the final amen.

articles.headline: Fourth quarter, same sermon: [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still 18.4 from salvation
paras: Fourteen minutes passed and the hymnal stayed open to the same page. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] sits on 51.9 with nobody left to play, and [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] holds at 70.3. The gap is still 18.4. Chop% is frozen too: Rise to the top stays at 100% by our numbers.

No new miracles from the back pew. [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] rests at 12.9, and the choir's projected finish cooled from 79.6 to 76.4. Upstairs, [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] is still buzzing on [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]] at 18.7, while [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] waits on [[p:11560|Caleb Williams (QB, CHI, #18)]] at 13.3.

Q4, 14:09, and the last live starters in our league all share one field. For the next chapter to flip, Torn-Again would need to lose 18.4 points in a quarter, and scoreboards don't take collections back. Rise to the top remains projected for the chop, one quarter from the final amen.

articles.headline: The collection plate goes backwards, and [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still can't reach it
paras: Hold the presses: a scoreboard took a donation back. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] slipped 0.7 to 69.6, the first movement at the bottom in a quarter-hour. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still sits on 51.9 with an empty bench of hope, so the gap shrinks to 17.7. Chop% doesn't blink: 100% for Rise to the top by our numbers.

Nobody new rang the bell. [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] holds at 12.9 and [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]] at 7.8, both still on the field for the choir, which is now projected to finish at 74.5. Up the aisle, [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]], [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] and [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] all wait on that same game, comfortably out of the splash zone.

Q4, 11:41. Last chapter said scoreboards don't take collections back. Turns out they take a little. For the next chapter to flip, Torn-Again would need to give back 17.7 more before the final whistle, and Swift and Loveland would have to go deep into the red together. Until then, Rise to the top stays projected for the chop, kneeling at the altar.

articles.headline: The choir hits the high note, and [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] is left alone at the altar
paras: So much for the collection plate going backwards. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] just passed it around again and came back 9.2 richer, climbing to 78.8 and leapfrogging [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] out of tenth. Down at the bottom, [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still kneels on 51.9 with nobody left to send in. The gap to safety is now 26.3. Chop%: 100, by our numbers, and it hasn't flinched all night.

The sermon came from [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]], who added 7.0 since the last chapter to reach 19.9. [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]] chipped in 2.2 to hit 10.0. Last chapter asked the pair to go deep into the red together. They went deep, all right, just the other direction.

Q4, 6:01. ZynFree has [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]] still on the field at 18.7, and the choir still has Swift and Loveland singing. The fight for ninth is only about pride now: Torn-Again projected 81.6, ZynFree projected 80.5. For the next chapter to flip, ZynFree would have to hand back 26.3 points before the final whistle. Until then, Rise to the top stays projected for the chop.

articles.headline: Two minutes left, and the only suspense is who sings louder for ninth
paras: The pews are full and the pulpit is empty. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] still sits on 51.9 with nobody left to send in, and the gap to safety just stretched to 30.9. Chop%: 100, by our numbers. The axe has stopped pretending to think about it.

Up front, the choir and the Zyn crowd traded hymns. [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]] added 6.8 more to reach 26.7, lifting [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] to 85.6. [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] answered with [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]], up 4.6 to 23.3, and climbed to 82.8. Last chapter asked ZynFree to hand back 26.3 points. Instead the cushion got thicker.

Q4, 2:16. Swift, Smith-Njigba and [[p:12517|Colston Loveland (TE, CHI, #84)]] are still on the field. Torn-Again is projected 86.8, ZynFree projected 83.7, so ninth is the only race left with a pulse. For it to flip, ZynFree needs 2.9 more than the choir before the whistle. For the chop to flip, it would take a miracle nobody has booked. Rise to the top stays projected for the block.

articles.headline: Monday's hymn lifts the choir past the insurance man as [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] falls
paras: The whistle has blown on Monday night, and with it on Week 8. Nobody has a starter left to send. Last chapter promised suspense only in the fight for ninth, and the choir delivered a twist nobody had in the hymnal.

[[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] won the day with 37.1 points, and the sermon belonged to [[p:6790|D'Andre Swift (RB, CHI, #4)]], who put up 27.1 today. The choir finished on 87.3. That did more than beat the Zyn crowd: it slipped past [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]], parked on 86.8 all day. The insurance policy covers a lot, but not getting passed while standing still. Naber slides to ninth by half a point.

[[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] answered with 23.3, all of it from [[p:9488|Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR, SEA, #11)]]. That left ZynFree on 82.8, tenth, 30.9 clear of the bottom. Not pretty, but on chop week, tenth is a fine seat.

Chicago's Monday crowd spread the wealth elsewhere too. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] banked 16.6 from [[p:12519|Luther Burden III (WR, CHI, #10)]] to close on 92.0. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] took 14.1 from [[p:11560|Caleb Williams (QB, CHI, #18)]] and finished on 88.8. Nobody got hurt on the night. Up top, [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] sat on 144.6 all day and never had to look down.

And now the farewell. [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] closes Week 8 on 51.9, the lowest total on the board, with a Chop% of 100 that has not budged in days. The name promised an ascent. The week delivered a long, quiet ride down to the block. Eleven teams walked into Week 8, and ten walk out. Rise to the top heads for the chopping block with our fondest salute, and the race rolls on without them.

articles.headline: [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] is gone; its roster hits the wire and ten teams start circling
paras: No games on a Tuesday, but the Chopping Block never really sleeps. Monday night's farewell became Monday night's paperwork: minutes after the whistle, [[t:josephfoster20|Rise to the top]] was chopped, and the whole roster went out the door with it. Eleven teams started Week 8. Ten report for Week 9.

That is a lot of talent suddenly looking for a home. [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] and [[p:10859|Sam LaPorta (TE, DET, #87)]] headline the pile, with [[p:5846|DK Metcalf (WR, PIT, #4)]] right behind them and a stack of starters any of the ten survivors would happily add. In a guillotine league, one team's misfortune is everybody else's shopping trip. No claims have landed yet. The race caller can see the shelves, not the carts.

One team did not wait for the wire to come to it. [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] cut [[p:5947|Jakobi Meyers (WR, JAX, #3)]] on Tuesday afternoon and cleared a seat. Third place last week at 113.3, nothing to sweat, and still tinkering. Hockey Guy may be lost at a football game, but somebody on that bench knows what an empty roster spot is for.

So the board resets. Last week's bottom was 51.9, and that number left with its owner. [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] holds the high ground after a 144.6 week. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] and [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] both got passed while standing still on Monday and will not want a repeat. Week 9 opens with ten teams, one axe, and a wire full of fresh ammunition. The next chapter is about who grabs it.

articles.headline: [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] pays a 769 FAAB premium; uninsured [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again]] is projected last
paras: The carts are in. Waivers ran overnight, and the race caller who could only see the shelves yesterday can now read the receipts. One team did not shop so much as buy the store's extended warranty.

[[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] finished at 86.8 last week and got passed standing still on Monday. The answer: 469 FAAB for [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] and another 300 for [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]], with two receivers shown the door to make room. That is 769 FAAB in one night. Like a good neighbor, Naber is now projected for 113.2 and a 5% Chop%. The premium comes due quickly: [[p:9997|Flowers]] plays Thursday, and [[p:11584|Irving]] follows on Sunday night.

The other pile headliner went cheaper. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] paid 51 for [[p:10859|Sam LaPorta (TE, DET, #87)]], swapping one tight end for another after an 88.8 week. Projected 107.8 now, with a 9% Chop%. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] changed tight ends too, for just 9. Meanwhile [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]], already projected to lead the field at 135.9, spent 27 on [[p:8183|Brock Purdy (QB, SF, #13)]] and let the old quarterback go. Some teams shop because they are hungry. This one is simply named that way.

And that empty seat at [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]]? Filled, for 6 FAAB, with a Denver receiver. Still lost at a football game, but apparently fluent in clearance racks. Projected 111.9, 6% Chop%, and nothing to sweat so far.

The real drama is what did not happen at the bottom. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] shows no claim on the sheet, one starter already out, and a projected 88.8 that is the lowest in the league. That comes with a 43% Chop%. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] sits next up at a projected 98.1 and 22%, also without a claim on the sheet. Faith is a fine thing to carry into Week 9, but the church crowd is the one team here working without a policy.

Ten teams, one axe, and the paperwork is finished. Thursday night is the first whistle, and a 300 FAAB receiver gets the first chance to prove the premium was worth paying. Next chapter, the receipts start scoring.

articles.headline: Kickoff: [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again]] fills the pew, and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] inherits the hot seat
paras: First whistle, and the board flipped before a single point landed. The church crowd that closed the last chapter uninsured and projected last? [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] now shows a full lineup, a projected 117.8, and a Chop% down from 43 to 7. Fourth from the bottom. Miracle or lineup fix, the caller only reads the sheet. Someone has to take the seat, and it slid under [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]]: projected 109.0, lowest on the board alongside [[t:MVeny|MVeny]], and an 18% Chop% that rose 12 points without a snap played.

Tonight's turn is Baltimore against Jacksonville. The 300 FAAB receiver gets his audition: [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]] is on the field for [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]], sixth at 11% and waiting for the policy to pay out. outsiderightfoot has [[p:3198|Derrick Henry (RB, BAL, #22)]] in the same huddle, its whole evening on the hot seat. [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] has two Jaguars running and nothing to sweat, projected 137.0 at under 1%.

Zeros everywhere, Q1 14:54. [[p:3198|Henry]] carries a hot seat on his back; one trip to the end zone shuffles the bottom again, and outsiderightfoot still holds [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] for late Monday. [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]], seventh at 11%, has nobody until Sunday and can only watch. Next chapter: the receipts start scoring, for real this time.

articles.headline: [[p:3198|Henry]] jogs 22 yards, the hot seat slides to [[t:MVeny|MVeny]], and the 300 FAAB policy pays 1.1
paras: Receipts, as promised, and the first one was tiny. [[p:3198|Derrick Henry (RB, BAL, #22)]] took four carries for 22 yards, 3.1 points, and that was enough: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] climbed off the bottom and [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] slid under it without playing a snap. Projected 109.0 against 109.1. One tenth of a point separates the hot seat from the next chair, both Chop% read 17, and the caller needs a magnifying glass.

The 300 FAAB policy filed its first claim: [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]] has one carry for 9 yards and one catch for minus 3. That is 1.1 points, and [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] slipped a chair, seventh to eighth, Chop% up to 14. Insurance is a long game. Meanwhile the team with nothing to sweat found a way to sweat less: [[p:12490|Bhayshul Tuten (RB, JAX, #33)]] turned five carries into 16 yards and a touchdown, and [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] leads the week at 9.7.

Q1, 2:00. [[p:3198|Henry]] is still in the huddle with the hot seat on his back, and every yard pushes MVeny deeper into a chair it never sat in. MVeny's answer waits until Sunday, when its seven starters wake at once. [[p:9997|Flowers]] has three quarters to make the policy look smart. Next chapter: does a one-tenth gap survive the half?

articles.headline: Claim denied: [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] slides two chairs to the hot seat, Chop% 18
paras: Put the magnifying glass away. The one-tenth gap survived the half, and it stopped mattering, because [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] slid under both chairs at once. [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]] has 1.8 points on two carries and a catch for minus 3, the projection sagged to 107.6, and the policyholder fell from eighth to the bottom. Chop% up four to 18. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] climbs to ninth without a snap, and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] sits in eighth with its hands in its pockets.

The turn was [[p:3198|Derrick Henry (RB, BAL, #22)]], who just kept grinding: 11 carries, 50 yards, 6.4 points, every one of them a little more daylight for outsiderightfoot. Up top, the team with nothing to sweat found a way to sweat less again. [[p:12490|Bhayshul Tuten (RB, JAX, #33)]] has eight carries and a touchdown, and [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] leads the week at 10.3, Chop% 1.

Q2, 3:03. [[p:9997|Flowers]] has a half and change to make the premium worth it: a couple of real catches push the projection back over MVeny's 109.0 and the chairs shuffle again. [[p:3198|Henry]] is still running, which does not help. The rest of the Naber policy, seven starters strong, does not wake until Sunday. Next chapter: does the insurance pay before the whistle, or does the caller need a bigger glass?

articles.headline: Henry grinds [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] into the pile: three chairs, nine tenths of a point
paras: Bigger glass, please. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] still holds the bottom chair at 108.1 projected, though the policy paid a little: [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]] took two carries for 16 yards, 2.8 points, and the Chop% eased to 17. The trouble is who fell in beside it. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] slid from eighth to ninth, projected 108.4, Chop% also 17. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] rises to eighth at 109.0 without a snap. Three chairs, nine tenths of a point.

The man pulling outsiderightfoot down is the one it leans on. [[p:3198|Derrick Henry (RB, BAL, #22)]] has 12 carries for 51 yards and 6.5 points, all grind and no end zone, and the projection sank under MVeny's. Up top, the sweat-free team sweats less still: [[p:9487|Parker Washington (WR, JAX, #11)]] turned two catches into 61 yards and a touchdown, and [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] leads at 21.8 with a Chop% that rounds to zero.

Q2, 0:22. Half a game left for [[p:9997|Flowers]] and [[p:3198|Henry]], pulling opposite ways: a Henry score lifts outsiderightfoot clear and leaves the Naber alone on the floor, while one real Flowers catch flips the chairs again. The rest of the bottom three sleeps until Sunday, when the Naber wakes seven starters at once. Next chapter: does the insurance pay before the whistle, or does the caller need a microscope?

articles.headline: [[p:3198|Henry]] throws a pass, loses three yards, and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] hits the floor
paras: Microscope it is. The chairs flipped: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] now sits on the bottom at 104.5 projected, Chop% up five to 21, while [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] climbs one chair to 105.2 and a Chop% of 19. The policy keeps paying in nickels: [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]] added a point since the last call, three carries and three catches for 23 yards combined. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] still sits eighth at 109.0 without taking a snap.

The turn was no turn at all. [[p:3198|Derrick Henry (RB, BAL, #22)]] has 16 carries for 55 yards, still no end zone, and the one new line on his sheet is a pass: one attempt, one completion, minus three yards. He lost a tenth of a point since the last chapter, and outsiderightfoot lost the chair. Up top, [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] added a second touchdown, this one from [[p:12490|Bhayshul Tuten (RB, JAX, #33)]], and leads at 22.5.

Q4, 13:35. Fifteen minutes left for [[p:3198|Henry]] and [[p:9997|Flowers]] to settle Thursday's seating. One Henry score lifts outsiderightfoot back over the Naber; another quiet quarter and it sleeps on the floor until Sunday, when both wake seven starters, the Naber's all at once and outsiderightfoot's stretching to [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] late Monday. Next chapter: a touchdown, or a tape measure?

articles.headline: Tape measure it is: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] sleeps on the floor by six tenths
paras: The bell rang on Thursday and nobody flipped a chair. [[p:3198|Derrick Henry (RB, BAL, #22)]] finished at 7.1 points with no touchdown, so the last chapter's question answered itself: tape measure. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] goes to bed on the bottom, projected 102.0 with a Chop% of 24. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] sits one chair up at 102.6 and 22. The gap between them is six tenths of a point, and nobody can touch it until Sunday.

The Naber's insurance policy paid out exactly as advertised: in nickels. [[p:9997|Zay Flowers (WR, BAL, #4)]] closed at 3.8, and that was the whole premium for the night. [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] banked 3.4 from its tight end and otherwise stayed out of the rain. Six teams, [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] among them, did not dress a single Thursday starter and watched from the cheap seats, which is where a hockey guy belongs at a football game.

Up top, a different sport entirely. [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] hung 22.5 on the board before most of the league had laced up, and the loudest line belonged to [[p:9487|Parker Washington (WR, JAX, #11)]]: two catches, 61 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. Henry needed sixteen carries and a pass attempt to reach 7.1. Washington needed two catches to nearly double it. nomnomnomnomnom leads at a projected 127.7 with a Chop% that rounds to 1.
The injury sheet from Thursday is blank. In this league, that counts as news.

So the microscope goes back in the drawer until Sunday morning, when the two floor-sitters wake up together. The Naber starts three in the early window, two in the late one and a running back Sunday night. outsiderightfoot answers with four early starters, one late, and still keeps [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] in its back pocket for late Monday, projected 23.1, the last card anyone at the bottom gets to play. Behind them, [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] sits eighth at 109.0 and a Chop% of 13 without having taken a snap, all seven starters due Sunday.
Six tenths of a point. Three days of waiting. Bring the tape measure.

articles.headline: Quiet Friday: the tape stretches and [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] goes shopping
paras: Not a snap was played on Friday, and the floor moved anyway. The projections shuffled overnight, and the six tenths of a point between the two bottom chairs stretched to a little over three. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] still sleeps on the bottom, now projected 101.6 with a Chop% of 26, up two and a half since Thursday's bell. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] drifted up to a projected 104.7 and watched its Chop% slip to 20. Same chairs, more daylight between them. Somebody check whether the tape measure is long enough.

The only move in the league came from the cheap seats. In the small hours of Friday, [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]], who did not dress a single Thursday starter, won a waiver claim for [[p:12474|Woody Marks (RB, HOU, #4)]] at 4 FAAB and sent Zach Charbonnet to the showers to make room. Marks skates straight into the Sunday late lineup, projected 16.4. A hockey guy at a football game may not know the rules, but he does know how to make a line change.

On paper, the line change worked. Hockey Guy slid two chairs toward the safe end of the room, from sixth to fourth, with a Chop% of 6, down nearly three. [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] went the other way without leaving the hangar: from second to fifth, projected 118.2, Chop% of 6, a little turbulence on an otherwise grounded afternoon. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] stayed parked in eighth at a projected 108.8 and a Chop% of 15, all seven starters still waiting on Sunday.

Up top, nothing to see. [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] keeps the 22.5 it banked Thursday and leads at a projected 127.3 with a Chop% that still rounds to 1. No trades, no other claims, no injuries. Nineteen managers stood pat and stared at the two floor-sitters. One went shopping.

Sunday morning, both floor-sitters wake up at once. outsiderightfoot opens with four early starters and still keeps [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] in its back pocket for late Monday, projected 22.8, the last card anyone at the bottom gets to play. The Naber answers with three in the early window, two late, and [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] under the Sunday night lights, projected 21.4, the policy's biggest premium.
Three points now. Two days of waiting. Bring the tape measure, and maybe a receipt.
